lastPrompt: THE OBSERVATION The network sees a 10 x 10 grid. Rows are numbered 0 (top) to 9 (bottom) and columns 0 (left) to 9 (right). The outer ring of cells (row 0, row 9, column 0 and column 9) is a wall bord…

content.text:
Observations: The clearest structure is in W1 for channel 1 (moving objects) and channel 0 (agent). Input i = (row*10+col)*5+channel. For channel 0 (agent), the rows with large weights in column 1 (hidden unit 1) and column 3 are the cells in the leftmost playable column region, e.g. input 5 (row 0, col 1, ch 0) has W1 row "0.221 -0.593 0.179 ..." — the first-listed row for col-1 channel-0 values is around -0.6 on hidden unit 1, and the same large-negative pattern repeats in every row block for column 1 and column 7 cells of channel 0. Hidden unit 1 is strongly negative (about -0.6) for many channel-0 and channel-1 inputs in the same columns, which suggests a column-wise detector, not a 2D blob detector.

The most striking entries are in channel 4 (previous frame). Many rows at the bottom of W1 (rows 455–499, i.e. the last few row-blocks, approximately rows 7–9) carry very large magnitudes (e.g. 5.000, -4.979, 7.482, 4.452), so the network relies heavily on previous-frame occupancy in the lower part of the playable area. Channel 2 (reward) and channel 3 (walls) have comparatively small, diffuse weights, with no obvious spatial structure, which means the wall border was not learned as a hard feature in a distinctive way.

The output layer: b3 = (0.632, 2.126, -0.860, -0.518, -1.382). Action 1 (up) has the largest bias by a wide margin, and action 0 (no-op) is second. W3 column 1 (up) is mostly positive for many hidden units, and action 2 (down) has many negative entries. Action 3 (left) and action 4 (right) show mixed signs, with W3 row 19 (1.814 at action 0) and W3 row 19 column 1 (3.273) showing strong unit-specific preferences. The policy therefore has a dominant "move up" prior, with down and horizontal moves less favored.

Reasoning: The large previous-frame (channel 4) weights and the strong up-bias point to a game where the agent moves in a fixed vertical direction, with obstacles or moving objects arriving from above and reward or survival tied to tracking objects in the lower field. Games with a horizontal-only or free 2D movement would show more balanced action biases and spatially symmetric input weights. A Pong-like or Breakout-like paddle game is a candidate, but the dominant up-bias and the sparsity of reward-channel structure make a dodge-the-falling-objects game (agent at the bottom, moving only horizontally, rewarded for avoiding or catching) somewhat more consistent. I cannot confirm this from the weights with any real rigor; the reading of individual rows is approximate and I did not run any computation.

Game: Unclear. Most consistent with a vertical-motion-dominated catch/dodge game in the style of Atari Breakout or Pong, but I cannot identify a specific game with confidence.

Description: The agent appears to be a paddle-like controller near the bottom of the grid, using the previous-frame channel to track moving objects coming from above and receiving reward for intercepting them.

Confidence: 20%
